title: Burst lightbox observability playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-facing playbook for investigating and instrumenting short-lived inference bursts (microbursts) and hallucination correlations. The goal is a lightweight "lightbox" investigators can open during an incident or rollout canary that immediately surfaces the right metrics, trace anchors, and ownership notes.

Context and motivation:
- Microbursts impact SLOs quickly and are expensive to debug because signals are high-cardinality and short-lived.
- Existing dashboards tend to be 'session-first' and miss transient burst anchors like KV-eviction spikes or sudden model fanout.
- This doc proposes a minimal metric set, trace annotation conventions, dashboard widgets, and a checklist to onboard feature rollouts and oncall flow.

Who should use this:
- Oncall: fast TTR (time to resolution) during token-latency spikes
- Release owners: rollout gating for new routing or quantization profiles
- Engineers instrumenting serving runtime: clear names and sampling budgets to implement

Compact metric glossary (definitions for quick instrument sanity checks):
- burst.start_rate: rate of requests per tenant within 30s window. Unit: req/s. Derived as a rolling 30s count / 30. Owner: routing team.
- burst.duration_p90: 90th percentile duration of contiguous high-rate window (start to recovery). Unit: seconds. Use for incident summaries. Owner: serving-runtime.
- token.latency.fanout_ms: time spent waiting for downstream model fanout (multi-model routing). Unit: ms per request. Tag by model_variant.
- kv.evictions_per_min: number of KV cache evictions per minute per host. High values -> cold prefixes.
- inference.fallback_rate: fraction of requests routed to fallback model/region. Unit: percent. Important for graceful degradation visibility.
- output.quality.alerts: counts of automated quality checks (prompt-set mismatches, hallucination heuristics). Not a replacement for offline evals but used as a signal.

Trace annotation conventions (lightweight):
- span.tag = {"burst_anchor": "true"} whenever burst.start_rate > configured tenant threshold. Include tenant_id and route.
- span.event = "kv_evict" attach key_prefix and eviction_reason when kv.evictions_per_min spikes.
- span.meta = {"model_variant":"vX", "cache_state":"cold|warm|stale"} encoded as simple tags to enable quick filtering.
- correlation_id: use request.session_id + short random suffix to stitch multi-hop traces; show TTL in span to avoid ambiguous cross-tenant joins.

Sampling policy suggestion (budgeted, severity-weighted):
- Default: 0.5% of all requests sample full traces.
- When burst.start_rate for a tenant crosses threshold: dynamically upsample to 10% for that tenant for 5 minutes.
- When output.quality.alerts increase by >3x: upsample to 50% for sample of requests that triggered alerts (attach prompt snapshot).
- Retain light-weight trace metadata (span tags) for 7d at full fidelity; persist full trace payloads for 3d by default.

Dashboard lightbox widgets (prioritized order when opening lightbox):
1) Burst summary strip (one-line): tenant, start_time, last_seen, current_rate, fallback_rate, kv_evictions_last_5m.
2) Heatmap: per-host token.latency.fanout_ms over last 30m with host and model_variant axis.
3) KV eviction timeline: evictions_per_min with overlay of cache_size and eviction_reason spikes.
4) Trace-sampled list: top 20 sampled traces (by burst likelihood) with quick links to trace view and prompt replay.
5) Quality overlay: output.quality.alerts correlated with burst.start_rate and fallback_rate (scatter plot).
6) Rollout gates panel: current rollout percent, recent Canary failures, automatic rollback events.

Operator quick-check checklist (first 5 minutes):
- [ ] Read burst summary strip: confirm tenant and route.
- [ ] Open heatmap: see whether latency concentrated on specific hosts or model variants.
- [ ] Inspect KV eviction timeline: cold start? eviction storms?
- [ ] Open 3 sampled traces (prefer traces with span.tag burst_anchor=true) and check where time is spent (fanout vs model execution vs network).
- [ ] Check inference.fallback_rate: is the system intentionally diverting traffic?
- [ ] If output.quality.alerts present, tag incident as potential quality regression and notify ML owner.

Rollout gating recommendations (pre-deploy checklist for product/engineers):
- Ensure new model variant emits model_variant tag and minimal span meta (cache_state).
- Add a probe that simulates moderate burst to measure kv.evictions_per_min sensitivity under test.
- Confirm sampling policy flags exist and are on by default in canary cluster.
- Add 1 synthetic probe metric mapped to rollout percent (synthetic.latency.canary) to detect immediate regressions.

Unresolved / open questions for follow-ups:
- What is the TTL for retaining sampled prompt snapshots in privacy-sensitive tenants? (policy needed)
- How to make burst thresholds tenant-aware (baseline-normalized) without adding heavy per-tenant computation?
- Should we centrally surface eviction_reason taxonomy (OOM, TTL, manual) and standardize names?

Implementation notes for infra/telemetry engineers:
- Prefer lightweight tags (strings) over large JSON baggage on spans to limit trace DB costs.
- Instrument eviction_reason as an enum; record counts as a counter metric and emit a single span.event on eviction tallies.
- A small sidecar can compute burst.start_rate per tenant and publish it as a metric; avoid re-computing in the serving hot path.

Owner and runbook fragments:
- Playbook owner: eng-serving-runtime (Priya Nair).
- Oncall escalation: SRE -> Serving Runtime -> ML Ops@20m if quality signals persist.

Notes to self / ad-hoc brainstorms (raw):
- Could add a lightweight 'burst fingerprint' for recurring bursts to help identify automation-induced loops.
- Consider a compact cached summary per tenant (last_burst_hash) to speed aggregation in dashboards.

References and links:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-1283 (burst detection design doc)
- Investigation ticket example: JIRA-INV-457
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/612

If you open the lightbox during an incident and something is missing, call out with the tag "lightbox-missing" in the incident doc so we can iterate. This doc is intentionally compact; follow the linked Confluence design doc for deep-dive instrumentation patterns.
